scenes.script_line: Imagine standing beside a large tree. Its trunk is wide. Its branches stretch overhead. You can feel the shade beneath it. Now ask yourself a simple question. How long has this tree been here? Perhaps it began growing before some of us were born. Perhaps people who worked on this land many years ago stood in the same shade. A tree reminds us that some things take a long time to grow.

scenes.script_line: And that what we do today can matter long after our working day has ended. Think about a wall built many years ago. The people who made it are no longer standing beside it. But their work remains. We can still see the decisions they made. How they placed the stones. How they cared for the details.

scenes.script_line: How the wall has lasted over time. Every builder leaves something behind. A structure. A path. A repair. A change in the landscape. The question is not whether we leave a mark. The question is what kind of mark we leave. During this course, we have learned that the land is alive. We have learned that waste does not disappear just because we stop looking at it.

scenes.script_line: We have looked beneath our feet and discovered why soil matters. We have followed water through the landscape. We have seen how small actions become patterns. We have learned to observe nature before we act. And we have discovered that regeneration means helping living places recover. These are different lessons. But they all lead to one idea.

scenes.script_line: What we care for today can grow tomorrow. Let's repeat. What we care for today can grow tomorrow. Imagine two people teaching someone new to the team. The first says, "Finish your work as fast as you can. Someone else will take care of the rest." The second says, "Do your work well. Protect the area. Put materials in the right place. Leave it ready for the next person."

scenes.script_line: Which message would you want a new worker to learn? Which habit would you want repeated a hundred times? We are always teaching through our actions. Even when we do not realise it. Now imagine the land here in ten years. Some buildings may be finished. Some young trees may have grown taller. Some parts of the landscape may have recovered well. Other parts will still need care. The future is not guaranteed by good intentions.

scenes.script_line: It is shaped by practical decisions, good planning and steady work. No single person can do everything. But each person can contribute something real. People arrive at Edenrise with different histories. Different skills. Different languages. Different ideas. But we share a place where we work. And we share a responsibility to the people who come after us. The next worker. The family who visits.

scenes.script_line: The child who walks beside a tree. The neighbour who lives downstream. When we protect this place, we are thinking beyond ourselves. Remember the standards we practise here. No litter left behind. No cigarette butts on the ground. No dumping, burning or burying of site waste. No dirty washwater into soil or drains. Respect protected trees, habitats and approved site boundaries.

scenes.script_line: Sort waste correctly. Report risks early. Finish each work area safely and cleanly. These are ordinary actions. But ordinary actions, repeated with care, can build something extraordinary. Take one moment now and imagine returning to this place many years from today. Perhaps you will point to a building and say, "I helped build that." That is something to be proud of. But imagine being able to say something more. "We built it carefully."

scenes.script_line: "We protected what was already here." "We left the place in good condition for the people who followed us." That is a deeper kind of pride. So let us remember the journey in three simple words. Notice. Care. Act. Again. Notice. Care. Act. Notice the world around you. Care about the consequences. Act in a way that protects the future.

scenes.script_line: Tomorrow, when you begin work, ask yourself one final question. "What will remain because I was here?" A mess for someone else? Or a job completed with care? A problem ignored? Or a problem prevented? A place treated carelessly? Or a place respected? Each day gives us new opportunities to choose. Because the legacy we leave behind is not made in one moment. It is made through the way we work, every day. What we care for today can grow tomorrow. And at Edenrise, that future belongs to all of us to protect.
